name: Court Interpreters
description: The most comprehensive directory of FCICE-certified and state-court-credentialed interpreters serving depositions, hearings, and client consultations across the United States.
certifications: NAJIT Member (National Association of Judiciary Interpreters and Translators)
DOJ EOIR Accredited Interpreter (Executive Office for Immigration Review)
RID CI (Registry of Interpreters for the Deaf — Legal/Court Specialist)
cityPagePromptContext: Court interpreters provide spoken language interpretation in legal settings including depositions, hearings, trials, and attorney-client meetings. Credentialed professionals (FCICE-certified, NCSC state court certified, EOIR-accredited) interpret simultaneously or consecutively across all legal proceedings. Attorneys and court administrators hire them for depositions, motion hearings, arraignments, family court proceedings, and immigration hearings. Assignments range from one-hour client consultations to multi-day trials. Certification status, language pair, and courtroom experience vary significantly and affect admissibility of interpreted testimony.
buyerSearchContext: when scheduling depositions, court hearings, client meetings, or immigration proceedings involving non-English-speaking parties

editorialAuthor.name: Nick Palmer
editorialAuthor.title: Founder & Lead Researcher
editorialAuthor.bio: Nick built this directory to help attorneys find credentialed court interpreters without relying on court-appointed lists that are often outdated or unavailable for depositions — a gap he ran into firsthand when sourcing a last-minute interpreter for a deposition with a Spanish-speaking witness.

schema.label: State Court Certified Interpreter
schema.scrape_hint: Look for state court certification numbers, mentions of passing the NCSC oral proficiency exam, or explicit "State Court Certified" designation on homepage, about page, or credentials section.

schema.label: Years of Experience
schema.scrape_hint: Extract from 'About Us', interpreter bios, or '15+ years in legal interpretation' statements; calculate from career start date or founding year if provided.

schema.label: Languages
schema.scrape_hint: Parse language list from homepage, services page, or interpreter profile; capture all listed source and target languages.

schema.label: Practice Areas
schema.scrape_hint: Parse services or specialties pages; look for explicit mentions of deposition, criminal, civil, family court, immigration, or administrative hearing interpretation.

schema.label: FCICE Certified (Federal Court)
schema.scrape_hint: Look for explicit "FCICE" credential, "Federal Court Interpreter Certified" designation, or certification by the Administrative Office of U.S. Courts on credentials or bio pages.

schema.label: Remote / VRI Available
schema.scrape_hint: Check for mentions of 'video remote interpretation', 'VRI', 'Zoom interpretation', 'remote legal interpreting', or virtual/telephonic service options on services or FAQ pages.

schema.label: Scheduling Availability
schema.scrape_hint: Extract from FAQs, booking pages, or service descriptions; look for rush or emergency availability language or standard lead-time requirements.

schema.label: Phone Number
schema.scrape_hint: Extract from header, footer, contact page, or click-to-call buttons; normalize to standard format (e.g., (555) 123-4567).

schema.label: Website
schema.scrape_hint: Capture primary domain from browser address bar, homepage links, or business listings; ensure full URL with https:// protocol.
